A1.title: Programme read-out: all 10 holdout DMAs
A1.story: The headline question: 4 weeks with branded paid search paused in 10 stratified-random DMAs (2 hubs, 4 regional, 4 drive-to), against 40 controls. All three macro estimators, then dollars.
A1.question: Was branded paid search incremental, and was it worth its spend?

stages.note: Truth (known, simulated): direct -2.47 and OTA 1.64 bookings per DMA-day from pausing.

stages.title: 2. Pre-period fit & placebo-in-time

metrics.label: MMT pre-fit error
metrics.help: RMSE of pre-period counterfactual vs observed, % of mean

metrics.label: Worst placebo drift
metrics.help: bookings per DMA-day of effect found where none exists

stages.note: A counterfactual that finds an effect 4 weeks before the pause is mis-calibrated by about that much.

chart.title: Direct bookings per holdout DMA-day (7-day mean)

stages.title: 3. Matched-market test (MMT)
stages.note: Ratio-adjusted matched control; no model, so it inherits any pre-period drift between a pair.

stages.title: 4. Synthetic DiD (SDID)
stages.note: Re-weights donors on their pre-period trend and re-weights pre-period days; the headline estimator.

stages.title: 5. Bayesian structural time series (BSTS)
stages.note: Forecasts the counterfactual from control-DMA principal components; shrinks toward zero here (see flow B1).

stages.title: 6. Economics (headline: SDID)

metrics.label: OTA commission leakage
metrics.help: commission paid on bookings diverted to OTAs

stages.note: Net contribution margin = direct GBV - SEM spend + OTA GBV x (1 - commission). Value of branded search = -(effect of pausing).

chart.title: ROAS: what last-click credits vs what is incremental

stages.title: 7. Verdict
stages.note: The direct loss is significant, but net value's interval spans zero: cannibalization is too uncertain to be decisive.

A1.action: The direct loss is significant, but net value's interval spans zero: cannibalization is too uncertain to be decisive.

A2.title: Read-out for the two Tier-1 hub holdouts
A2.story: Same experiment, but only the two major hubs, the markets where OTA conquesting is fiercest. Two treated DMAs can never produce a permutation p below 0.5, so the stage metrics show what thin evidence looks like.
A2.question: Was branded paid search incremental, and was it worth its spend?

stages.title: 7. Verdict
stages.note: With 2 treated DMAs the exact permutation test cannot go below p = 0.50, and the three estimators disagree (-8.9 to -7.9 per DMA-day). The point estimate leans KEEP ($163,655); the simulated truth, -$5,127, shows why not to act on it.

B1.title: Refutation suite on direct bookings
B1.story: Placebo-in-time, placebo-in-space and a Monte-Carlo over fresh experiments, to decide which of MMT, SDID and BSTS to believe.
B1.question: Can we trust these estimates, and which estimator should we believe?

stages.title: 1. What is being refuted
stages.note: Each estimator must find nothing where nothing happened, and must be roughly unbiased across fresh experiments.

stages.title: 2. Placebo-in-time (pause 4 weeks early, pre-data only)
stages.note: The true placebo effect is 0. An interval excluding zero means pre-period drift the estimator cannot absorb.

stages.title: 3. Placebo-in-space (fake-treat control DMAs)

metrics.label: Placebo ATT sd
metrics.help: 300 fake holdouts drawn from control DMAs

metrics.label: p (SDID estimate)
metrics.help: share of placebo effects at least as extreme

stages.note: If the real effect sits far in the tail of the placebo distribution it is unlikely to be luck.

stages.title: 4. Monte-Carlo over fresh experiments
stages.note: New DMAs and new randomisation each time; bias and coverage are the honest scorecard.

chart.title: Monte-Carlo bias in direct bookings per DMA-day (estimate - truth)

stages.title: 5. Headline seed against truth
stages.note: Truth -2.47. One draw proves little; stages 2-4 are what decide trust.

stages.title: 6. Verdict
stages.note: MMT: CAUTION (placebo-in-time finds a false effect); SDID: PASS; BSTS: FAIL (Monte-Carlo bias +2.12 is large vs truth -2.47; CI coverage only 60%)

B1.action: MMT: CAUTION (placebo-in-time finds a false effect); SDID: PASS; BSTS: FAIL (Monte-Carlo bias +2.12 is large vs truth -2.47; CI coverage only 60%)

B2.title: Refutation suite on OTA bookings
B2.story: The same suite on the OTA-diversion outcome. OTA volume is smaller and noisier, so the placebo bands are wider.
B2.question: Can we trust these estimates, and which estimator should we believe?

D1.title: Pause iff gain > 1 x learner disagreement
D1.story: The default policy, with its margin fixed before looking at the truth: pause a DMA only when the nine learners' mean gain exceeds one standard deviation of their disagreement.
D1.question: Which DMAs should pause, and does the rule actually pay?

stages.title: 1. Rule definition

metrics.label: Rule
metrics.value: pause iff mean gain - 1 x sd > 0

metrics.label: Out-of-fold
metrics.help: each DMA is scored by models that never saw it

stages.note: Gain = predicted d(net contribution margin) per day from pausing, computed per learner then combined.

stages.title: 2. Learner agreement

metrics.label: Unanimous on sign
metrics.help: DMAs where all 9 learners agree pause vs keep

stages.note: Large disagreement relative to the gain is the signal the margin k is meant to respect.

stages.title: 3. Decisions
stages.note: Counts of Pause decisions against the ground-truth oracle.

stages.note: Scoring uses simulated truth that a live test never has; in practice use a doubly robust policy-value estimate.

stages.title: 5. Cost of being wrong
